hero.h1: Freelance web developer in Paris and Île-de-France
hero.lead: L'Échoppe du Code is my independent web development workshop. I'm Ludovic Bataille, your single point of contact from scoping to launch: custom code, delivered with its sources, and a site that belongs to you outright.
hero.facts: Marketing websites from €2,600, online shops from €6,500, business applications from €9,500. Each package is a foundation priced in days; specific needs are added as modules. Optional scoping from €290, half of which is set off against development. Registered non-profits get 50 % off. All prices exclude VAT.

method.eyebrow: From concept to launch, zero detours.
method.intro: No endless meetings, no guesswork. Every stage comes with a clear deliverable, a firm deadline, and a fixed price.
method.block1_text: You pitch your business needs. I tell you straight away if it's doable, which tech fits best, and exactly what it costs. If the project is still to be defined, we start with a scoping session.
method.block2_text: I design, I code. You stay focused on your business while I build. No time-wasting syncs — just tangible progress.
method.block3_text: A battle-tested, secure tool that is 100% yours. I walk you through the essentials, then get out of your way.

scoping.section_title:
Define the project
before building it
scoping.intro: A poorly scoped project always costs more to fix than to design. Before the first line of code, we settle the architecture, the scope, the compliance requirements and the business model. You leave with a report that belongs to you — one any developer can execute, including someone other than me.
scoping.condition: Optional for a brochure site. Required as soon as there are user accounts, online payment or sensitive data: I cannot quote seriously without it.
scoping.design_note: For projects still to be invented: features, business rules, content structure, economic model. The number of days is set by the scoping work.
scoping.vat_notice: The report is yours in every case. Where a development quote is signed within three months, 50 % of the scoping fee is set off against it.

portfolio.section_title: Six projects started. Six projects shipped.
portfolio.intro: Production-ready applications that run on their own — no hand-holding required. The list closes on my very first build: the distance travelled is part of the shop window.
portfolio.project1_desc: A Mina and Ewe learning platform for the Togolese diaspora. Protected course materials, one-on-one sessions with a teacher, real-time messaging, subscriptions and a bookshop — in three languages, from the first screen down to the invoices.
portfolio.project1_build1: Two payment rails, one ledger: card payments in euros via Stripe, mobile money in CFA francs via CinetPay — order settlement is written once, server-side.
portfolio.project1_build2: Compliant invoicing: invoices and credit notes on two continuous numbering series, archived PDFs, whole-franc amounts on the CFA rail.
portfolio.project1_build3: Self-maintaining Cal.com booking: the webhook re-registers on every startup, a half-hourly sweep catches missed cancellations, a new teacher's room is created in one click.
portfolio.project1_build4: A complete transactional mail service in three languages, every time read on the recipient's clock — session reminders, subscription lifecycle, payments refused by the bank — with a send log in the database, purged after twelve months.
portfolio.project1_build5: Double opt-in newsletter: one Resend audience per language, one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058), and a campaign trigger where you arm, then fire — a check first verifies the unsubscribe link is in the letter.
portfolio.project1_challenge: Two tills in two currencies had to produce a single set of books: order settlement is written once, server-side — and the CFA franc, which has no cents, forced whole-franc amounts all the way into the PDF invoices.
portfolio.project1_stat_label: automated tests against a real database
portfolio.project1_stack: Next.js 16 · NestJS · PostgreSQL · Prisma · Stripe · Socket.io
portfolio.project2_desc: A platform that runs a local farm co-op end to end: weekly baskets, members and producers, distribution shifts, treasury, PDF contracts and newsletters — live in production, built to be run by volunteers.
portfolio.project2_build1: Contract prices are never typed by hand: a single server-side pricing grid feeds the public form and the signed PDF contract alike, with a cheque breakdown exact to the cent.
portfolio.project2_build2: Treasury at paper pace: every cheque follows its cycle — in hand, at the bank, cashed or rejected — with a reminder to the member 30 days before deposit and a remittance list for the treasurer.
portfolio.project2_build3: Mail doesn't stop at sending: a Brevo webhook reports each message's actual fate, suppresses bouncing addresses and cuts the newsletter on a spam complaint.
portfolio.project2_build4: The weekly basket is generated from the seasonal catalogue, absent farms excluded from the draw, publication notified to active subscribers.
portfolio.project2_build5: Rich-text newsletters with batch sending, scheduling and drafts; a publication interrupted mid-send resumes on restart, without writing twice to addresses already served.
portfolio.project2_challenge: The real challenge wasn't technical: the tool is run by an association's volunteer board. Hence a built-in guide, screen by screen, and safeguards that refuse to start on an incomplete configuration rather than break down later.
portfolio.project2_stat_label: scheduled jobs running on their own
portfolio.project3_desc: End-to-end e-commerce for an Afro hair salon: a bilingual shop — the Love Your Curls line and jewellery —, Stripe payments, Brevo newsletters, and an admin space that holds it all, from orders to salon opening hours.
portfolio.project3_build1: No overselling possible: stock is checked before the Stripe session opens and decremented in a single atomic write — two customers can't buy the last item at the same time.
portfolio.project3_build2: Full or partial refunds from the admin: line items picked one by one, an immediate Stripe refund, a credit note generated on the spot with negative amounts, and an email to the customer.
portfolio.project3_build3: A built-in shipping chain: a CSV export ready for Colissimo Entreprise, and entering the tracking number marks the order shipped while sending the customer their tracking link.
portfolio.project3_build4: Abandoned carts don't freeze stock: a nightly sweep cancels orders unpaid for 24 hours and puts their items back on the shelf.
portfolio.project3_build5: A unified mail service: transactional emails on a shared base — email verification, welcome, order confirmation, shipping —, Tiptap newsletters through Brevo, and an HMAC-signed unsubscribe link: no unsubscribing someone else by tampering with the URL.
portfolio.project3_challenge: Two customers on the last item, a promo code redeemed twice at the same instant, two credit notes claiming the same number: every critical race was closed in the database — serializable transactions and conditional writes — rather than in the interface.
portfolio.project3_stat_label: before an abandoned cart returns its stock
portfolio.project4_desc: A community anime library, built solo: a catalogue imported from MyAnimeList, a six-status personal library, starred reviews, member submissions and an admin panel with moderation.
portfolio.project4_build1: Automated import from MyAnimeList via the Jikan API: the catalogue starts with 100 anime, an admin imports a pre-filled sheet in seconds, and DeepL translates synopses before they reach the database.
portfolio.project4_build2: Moderated contribution: any member can submit an anime — the entry waits in a moderation queue, pending, approved or rejected, before joining the catalogue.
portfolio.project4_build3: A six-status personal library with episode tracking: the progress bar advances, and an anime flips to "Finished" on its own when the last episode is marked.
portfolio.project4_build4: Layered security: differentiated rate limiting — free reads, limited writes —, honeypot anti-bot fields, IDOR protection: everyone edits only their own data.
portfolio.project4_build5: Accounts with email verification and one-hour reset tokens (Resend), user and admin roles, and an undeletable Super Admin.
portfolio.project4_challenge: Building a living catalogue on a third party's data: the Jikan import pre-fills, DeepL translates within a metered monthly quota, moderation filters — and if the translation key is missing, the site carries on in English rather than breaking.
portfolio.project4_stat_label: anime in the catalogue on day one
portfolio.project4_stack: Next.js 16 · Express · PostgreSQL · Prisma · Jikan API
portfolio.project5_desc: Showcasing a family estate nestled in the lush greenery of Montignac-Lascaux. For these three flower-named apartments, the goal was to craft a digital presence as warm as their gardens, ready to welcome travelers from all over the world.
portfolio.project5_build1: Five languages — French, English, Italian, Spanish, Dutch — with the choice persisted in the URL and the browser, for guests from all over Europe.
portfolio.project5_build2: No cookies, no trackers: GDPR compliance held by emptiness rather than by a banner — there is nothing to consent to.
portfolio.project5_build3: SEO built for a place: JSON-LD structured data, hreflang across five languages, a sitemap, and an llms.txt introducing the estate to AI crawlers.
portfolio.project5_build4: Apartment cards aligned with CSS subgrid, scroll-reveal animations via IntersectionObserver — no animation library.
portfolio.project5_challenge: Restraint as the brief: no back end, no cookie, no surplus framework — a five-language static site that loads fast and ages well, for owners with nothing to administer.
portfolio.project5_stat_label: languages, from the homepage to the legal pages
portfolio.project5_stack: React 19 · TypeScript · Vite · react-i18next · CSS Modules
portfolio.project6_desc: An artisan leather goods shop, and my very first build — kept here as it was. Stripe payments with webhooks, partial refunds detected automatically, PDF invoices, delivery tracking with an animated timeline: it is all already there, built while learning the trade.
portfolio.project6_build1: Already the foundations of the builds that followed: a signed Stripe webhook, stock validated server-side before payment, decremented after settlement and restored after a refund.
portfolio.project6_build2: Partial and full refunds detected by webhook, with stock restored and an email to the customer — the mechanism Fairy Chair Studio would later refine with credit notes.
portfolio.project6_build3: Dual-token sessions: a 15-minute access token, a 7-day refresh token with automatic rotation, and an anti-loop guard for requests expiring at the same moment.
portfolio.project6_build4: Delivery tracking across eight carriers: numbers validated by pattern, tracking URLs generated, shipping and delivery dates set automatically, an animated timeline client-side.
portfolio.project6_challenge: This is where I learned. The colours and the interface date from my beginnings, and I own them: this build stays online as the starting point. The distance between this page and Miabelangue is the whole journey this portfolio documents.
portfolio.project6_stat_label: files reworked in a full refactoring pass

about.p1: After 18 years leading teams and running field operations, I hung up the tie to come back to my true obsession: the raw mechanics of the web.
about.p2: Those years as a manager left me with a sharp, practical lens. I know business owners don't have time for jargon — they need tools that work. I have an eye for friction. I can tell immediately what's slowing your users down, what's making an interface feel heavy, or where something just rings false.
about.p3: That's what this Échoppe is built on. No hollow promises. What brings us together is a brief to honor and a result to deliver.
about.p4: We align on the foundations, I forge the architecture, and I don't close my editor until the machine does exactly what was agreed upon. My job is to write solid code so you can focus on yours.
